subtopics.title: What Globalisation Is — and the Forces That Caused It

questions.question: The lesson's working test for globalisation is that:
options: Decisions on one continent change prices, jobs and incomes on another, faster than a generation ago
Every country produces everything it needs

questions.question: The shipping container drove globalisation by:
options: Collapsing the cost of moving goods — one standard box from ship to truck to train without unpacking

questions.question: A firm slicing production into stages placed wherever each is cheapest creates a:
Which cause belongs to the POLICY family rather than the technology family?
options: Tariff reductions leading to the WTO in 1995

questions.question: South Africa's motor industry is cited as a gain from globalisation because:
options: It only sells inside South Africa
Global carmakers built world-scale plants here, supporting over 100 000 jobs
It is protected from all trade

questions.question: The clothing towns of Newcastle and parts of the Western Cape illustrate:
options: The losses column — jobs destroyed when cheap imports arrived after tariffs fell

questions.question: The 2008 crisis reached South African workers because:
options: The rand was fixed to the dollar
Our customers' economies stopped buying — financial contagion through an interconnected system

questions.question: The 'race to the bottom' refers to:
options: Mobile multinationals playing governments against each other on taxes and standards, while less mobile workers lose bargaining power
Countries competing to cut prices of exports

questions.question: The North/South divide labels are described as:
options: Strict geography — everything below the equator is South
Economic shorthand — Australia is southern on the map but Northern in the economy

questions.question: The terms-of-trade treadmill means many Southern economies:
options: Set world prices for their exports
Find their raw exports buying fewer and fewer manufactured imports over time

questions.question: The debt mechanism squeezes Southern budgets when:
options: World interest rates rise or their currencies fall, ballooning foreign-currency repayments
The IMF cancels all debts yearly

questions.question: Higher tariffs on processed goods than on raw materials historically discouraged the South from:

subtopics.title: South Africa Inside the Global Economy

questions.question: South Africa's openness is evidenced by:
options: Exports plus imports amounting to well over half of GDP

questions.question: The AfCFTA is described as the great opportunity because:
options: It removes all taxes in South Africa
Africa buys South Africa's manufactured goods, not just its ores

questions.question: 'South Africa is the North/South divide in one country' because:
options: Our provinces trade with different continents
The north of the country is richer than the south
Northern-style finance thrives in Sandton while exports stay raw-commodity dependent
We belong to no trade blocs

questions.question: The two-handed policy debate weighs deeper integration against:
options: Strategic protection — tariffs and local-content rules while industries rebuild

questions.question: The phone-as-map exercise shows a single phone touching at least:
options: Six countries across design, materials, assembly and connectivity

questions.question: Door one — 'it had to become possible' — was opened by:
options: Containers making goods cheap to move and cables making information instant

questions.question: South Africa walked back through door two — 'allowed to move' — when it:
options: Rejoined world markets and investors after 1994

subtopics.title: One Shop Now — Who Won and Who Lost on Our Streets

questions.question: Cheap imports are called 'a raise nobody announces' because:
options: Employers must raise wages by law
The same wage buys more when world-shop prices are lower

questions.question: The Newcastle story shows that trade's losses land on:
options: Whoever competes head-on with the world's cheapest producers

questions.question: 'Connected means exposed' summarises:
options: How a foreign crisis like 2008 travels to South African jobs within a year

questions.question: The economist's answer to 'is globalisation good or bad?' is that it:
options: Grows the total while moving the shares — so policy must spread gains and cushion losses

subtopics.title: Top of the Map, Bottom of the Map

questions.question: In the coffee-cup story, the South earns cents while the North earns rands because:
options: Coffee cannot grow in the North
The finishing — roasting, branding, retail — is where the money lives, and it happens up north

questions.question: The three weights on the South named in this section are:
options: Raw-for-made trade, foreign-currency debt, and weak voice in rule-writing institutions

questions.question: The African free trade agreement is 'the South's most direct answer' because it aims to:
options: Raise tariffs against all imports permanently
Move African economies to the North
Keep the finishing — and the rands — inside Africa by letting Africa sell made goods to Africa

questions.question: Which development is MOVING the North/South map?
options: China and India pulling the world's economic centre southward, and BRICS pressing for Southern voice
The North giving up manufacturing entirely
